question: Where can I get the locations of known mineral deposits and occurrences in the United States, with commodity, size or grade, and status (explored, mined, abandoned)?

answer.summary: USGS MRDS is the national point inventory: 266,599 US mines, prospects and occurrences with commodity and development status, but systematic updates stopped in 2011 and position precision varies. Tonnage and grade exist only in its relational tables for about 2,100 US records. USGS USMIN (13 critical-mineral commodities) and the Critical Mineral Deposits compilation (1,271 deposits, ver. 3.0, 2026) add dated status, resources and grade; Alaska's ARDF and state surveys such as Nevada's add regional detail.
main_caveats: MRDS has had no systematic updates since 2011; its dev_stat is the status at data entry and does not show whether a site is operating today.
MRDS positions range from 7.5-minute map plots to imprecise report locations; USGS says about 4,000 records have no reliable coordinates.
Size and grade are in separate relational tables (Resources, Resource_detail) for about 2,100 of 266,599 US MRDS records; the flattened CSV has neither.
Grades can be sample, production or resource figures; USMIN states older estimates may not follow NI 43-101 or JORC, so they are descriptive only.
USMIN deposits cover 13 critical-mineral commodities only; its WFS layer lists features (deposits, mines, districts) without status or resources.
ScienceBase (hosting USMIN packages and Critical Mineral Deposits ver. 3.0 files) returned HTTP 403 to automated curl requests in this test.
answer.confidence_reason: MRDS, USMIN WFS and ARDF were downloaded and counted; ScienceBase files, OSM and most state surveys were not tested.

attributes.note: MRDS: 266,599 US points (6 without coordinates); USMIN: 550 points, 481 polygons; ARDF: 7,425 Alaska points. Precision varies per record.
MRDS commod1-3 (names; commod1 blank in 17,224 US rows), USMIN commodity list, ARDF comm_main/comm_other, Nevada COM_MAJOR.
Tonnage tables cover about 1,900 US MRDS deposits plus USMIN critical-mineral records; MRDS prod_size is only an S/M/L or Y/N flag.
attributes.gap_note: No size or tonnage for about 99% of MRDS US records (flattened CSV has none). Critical Mineral Deposits ver. 3.0 files were not opened (ScienceBase returned 403 to curl).

attributes.note: MRDS Resource_detail grades for about 2,090 US deposits (wt-pct, g/mt); USMIN grade and cut-off for critical-mineral deposits.
attributes.gap_note: No grade for about 99% of MRDS US records; grades mix sample, production and resource bases, so they are not comparable without the record context.

attributes.note: MRDS dev_stat (Occurrence, Prospect, Producer, Past Producer, Plant, Unknown) on all US rows; USMIN history table adds dated status; ARDF status.

key_fields.meaning: Unique 8-digit record id; links to the full report at show-mrds.php?dep_id=<id> and to the relational tables.
Site name and WGS84 coordinates; precision varies by record.
Place names; country == 'United States' selects 266,599 rows.
Commodity names; each field can hold a comma-separated list (e.g. 'Copper, Gold, Silver').
Development status: Occurrence, Prospect, Producer, Past Producer, Plant or Unknown, as entered.
One-letter production-size flag (S, M, L or Y, N, U); populated in 81,821 US rows.
Operation type (Surface, Underground, Placer, Processing Plant, Unknown, ...), not an operator name.
Record-quality grade A (most information) to E.
Tonnage per deposit and year in rdbms-tab-all.zip.
Grade per commodity and year in rdbms-tab-all.zip.

how_to_use.example_request: curl -sL -o mrds-csv.zip https://mrdata.usgs.gov/mrds/mrds-csv.zip && unzip mrds-csv.zip  # then, in python3: csv.DictReader(open('mrds.csv', newline='')) and keep rows where country == 'United States'
how_to_use.example_result: {'dep_id': '10012285', 'site_name': 'Tyrone Mine', 'latitude': '32.6404', 'longitude': '-108.37284', 'state': 'New Mexico', 'county': 'Grant', 'commod1': 'Copper, Gold, Silver', 'dev_stat': 'Producer', 'prod_size': 'L', 'score': 'A'}  (266,599 US rows of 304,632)
steps: Download mrds-csv.zip (25,791,223 bytes) and read mrds.csv (137,239,557 bytes unzipped, UTF-8, 304,632 rows).
Filter country == 'United States' (266,599 rows) and optionally state, commod1-3 and dev_stat.
Open the url column (show-mrds.php?dep_id=...) for the full report, which lists production statistics and reserves/resources with grade.

For tonnage and grade in bulk, read Resources.txt and Resource_detail.txt from rdbms-tab-all.zip (123,559,542 bytes; supports HTTP Range, so single entries can be read from its central directory) and join on dep_id.

WFS alternative: https://mrdata.usgs.gov/services/wfs/mrds?request=GetFeature&service=WFS&version=1.1.0&typeName=mrds&resultType=hits returns numberOfFeatures=304632; the WFS bbox axis order is lat,lon.
reading_traps: commod1 is not a single commodity: it can hold a comma-separated list; commod1 is blank in 17,224 US rows.
dev_stat is the status when the record was entered (updates stopped in 2011); 'Producer' does not mean operating today.
prod_size has no tonnage meaning (two historical schemes, S/M/L and Y/N); blank in 184,778 US rows.
Size and grade are absent from the flattened CSV; only about 1,892 US records have any tonnage and 2,091 any grade in the relational tables (union 2,127).
'Plant' rows (1,204 in the US) are processing plants, not deposits; oper_type is not an operator name.
The default python-urllib client got HTTP 403 from mrdata.usgs.gov while curl worked.

evidence.quote: Grade, tonnage, and extent of mineralization essentially unknown.

how_to_use.example_result: site_id NV00123, ftr_id Mr00035, ftr_name Potosi Mining District, ftr_type Mining District, commodity tungsten, pt_def 'Approximate center of the polygon', loc_scale 'Small (<1:250,000)', loc_date 1998, state NV
steps: Count or fetch features from the WFS layers points, polygons or workings (typeName=points; resultType=hits for counts).

For status and resources open the record page https://mrdata.usgs.gov/deposit/show-deposit.php?id=<ftr_id>&f=html (example W-Mf00422: production 337,000 short ton units WO3, 1943 to 1957; history 'Active' 1945 to 1957).
Find ids with the search form: https://mrdata.usgs.gov/deposit/search.php?critical=W&state=NV returned 55 distinct feature ids.
For bulk tables with history, resources and production, the per-commodity CSV, shapefile and geodatabase packages are linked from the landing page (hosted on ScienceBase; not downloaded here).
reading_traps: The WFS 'points' layer includes mining districts and mines as well as deposits; filter on ftr_type and ftr_group.
WFS points are returned in EPSG:4267 (NAD27) in the sample response; MRDS uses WGS84.
Status and resources are not WFS attributes; they require the record pages or the commodity packages.
Search-form parameters take short values (critical=W, state=NV); a guessed value such as critical=Tungsten returned HTTP 500.
The landing page lists 13 commodity packages (incl. germanium) while the search form lists 12 critical-mineral options.

problems: Per-commodity packages are hosted on sciencebase.gov, which returned HTTP 403 to automated curl requests, so they were not downloaded.
